metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully navigated to Thunderbird Account Settings, entered a 2-line plain text signature 'Anonym\nXYZ Lab', and closed settings to save.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Account Settings, locate Signature text field, type multi-line text, and close settings to persist.
metadata.task_rationale: Harder than the source task: extends to 3 lines by adding a contact email. Tests that the agent correctly presses Enter twice for an extra line. Reuses same account/profile but checks all 3 lines.
metadata.explanation: Evaluator reads prefs.js after Thunderbird closes and applies a regex that must match all 3 newline-separated lines of the signature. The escaped dot in the email prevents regex wildcard matching.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter get_vm_file correctly fetches prefs.js from the VM and returns a local file path (str or None for single-file non-multi config).
Metric check_thunderbird_prefs correctly handles None result (returns 0.0) and opens the prefs file to parse user_pref lines.

The expected rule directly accesses mail.identity.id1.htmlSigText with method 're.S' and regex 'Anonym\nXYZ Lab\ncontact@xyz\.edu', which correctly matches all 3 required lines separated by literal newlines.
The escaped dot in 'xyz\.edu' prevents regex wildcard matching — semantically correct.
Postconfig closes the Thunderbird window before reading prefs.js, ensuring the file is flushed to disk before the getter reads it.
The expected.type='rule' pattern is handled correctly: the metric receives the rules dict directly and accesses 'expect'/'unexpect' keys without wrapping errors.
Static type warning (str vs Union return) is benign at runtime because the single-file path returns str or None, both handled by the metric.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding an 'unexpect' rule checking 'mail.identity.id1.htmlSigFormat': true to explicitly verify the signature is plain text (not HTML). Without this, an HTML-format signature containing the same 3-line text would incorrectly pass.
